units.title: Lines 1–2
units.summary: Line 1 (monumental script) is Shabaqo's full titulary carved as two mirrored halves running outward from a central ankh: Horus, Two Ladies and Golden Horus names (all Sbq-tꜣwy), Dual King Neferkare, Son of Re [Shabaqo], beloved of Ptah (left) / Sokar (right) South-of-his-Wall, living like Re forever. Line 2 is the dedication: the king found the ancestors' writing worm-eaten and illegible and had it copied anew in Ptah's temple.

words.gloss: Golden Horus (falcon on gold collar, G8 written as G5+S12)
Ptah (god's name written first: honorific transposition before mry)
like Re (Rꜥ written before mj; honorific/graphic transposition, same on the right end)
Sokar (right half substitutes Sokar for Ptah, as Sethe noted)
by (agentive jn; Sethe's copy has M17+N35 here)
words.note: Sethe translates as active 'Seine Majestät schrieb'

words.gloss: anew (n for m, as Sethe notes)

words.note: its last sign is lost in the damaged patch
Sethe: 'damit sein Name dauere'; two ḏd-pillars as drawn by Sethe and Breasted

units.title: Column 3
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: First preserved line of the theological text: Ptah is identified with 'this [land]' and said to be proclaimed with the great name [Tate]nen. Upper and lower parts are blank/erased; only a block of ~20 signs in the middle survives.

words.note: Sethe assumes tꜣ 'land' (a single stroke in the Vorlage) was dropped before pn; no trace of it on the stone.
Only the -nn survives; the name is restored from 13c.

units.title: Column 4
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Continues the Memphite identification: the land of Upper and Lower Egypt; the Uniter of this [land] appeared as King of Upper and King of Lower Egypt (the last clause written in two parallel half-columns).

words.gloss: the land of Upper and Lower Egypt
words.note: Two city determinatives (O49) after the two plant signs.

units.title: Column 5
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Entirely blank. Sethe (1928) explains this as a deliberate vacat by Shabaqo's scribe marking a large worm-eaten lacuna in the old original; the stone confirms that no line of text was ever carved here (or that nothing survives).

units.title: Column 6
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Isolated fragment set in mid-column with blank space above and below (Sethe: 'freier Raum'): 'the one who begot himself', so said Atum, 'who bore the Ennead'. Acknowledges Ptah as self-created creator.

words.note: Introduces the speaker after a quotation.
N9 doubtful; nine flags in three groups.

units.title: Column 7
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Short narrative fragment set in mid-column: the Ennead gathered to him (Geb), and he judged between Horus and Seth. Leads into the division of Egypt in col. 8.

words.note: Reed + leg; reading uncertain, Sethe notes the unusual arrangement.

units.title: Column 8
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Full-length narrative line: Geb prevents the quarrel and installs Seth as King of Upper Egypt in Su, where he was born, and Horus as King of Lower Egypt where his father was drowned (continues into col. 9 with the place name Psšt-tꜣwj).

units.title: Column 9
units.section: Ptah, king of the Two Lands
units.summary: Ends the division narrative: [Horus king] in Pesheset-tawy; so Horus and Seth each stood on a place and were content regarding the Two Lands in Ayan - 'that is the boundary of the Two Lands' (the last phrase written twice). Text stops at y~2450; the rest of the column is blank (Sethe: 'Absatz').

words.note: Sethe 'in bezug auf die beiden Länder'.
Here written with t instead of ṯ.

units.title: Column 10
units.summary: Geb's first speech in the dialogue (10a: to Seth, sending him to his birthplace), the scene notes Seth / Upper Egypt (10b), and the start of the narrative on Geb's dissatisfaction with an equal division (10c).

words.note: X1+G43; reading twt “resemble” as in Sethe, final t not written separately

units.title: Column 11
units.summary: Geb's second speech (11a: to Horus, sending him to the place where his father drowned), the scene notes Horus / Lower Egypt (11b), and the narrative of Geb giving his whole inheritance to Horus (11c).

words.note: V22 with complement m before and w-chick after

units.title: Column 12
units.summary: Geb's third speech (12a: to Horus and Seth together, 'I have separated you'), the scene notes (12b: field 1 blank, field 2 Lower and Upper Egypt), and the end of the narrative sentence identifying Horus as son of Geb's first-born (12c).

words.note: placed at the lower left of the addressee group, as in 10–18
reading uncertain; Sethe takes G43+Q3 with the preceding

units.title: Column 13
units.summary: First of six parallel columns of Geb's speech to the Ennead (13a 'I have appointed…', 13b Horus / 'you as the wtw-jackal'), with the narrative 13c on Horus standing as king and the land united under the name Tatenen South-of-his-Wall, lord of eternity.

words.note: addressee written against the text direction; D58 (b of Gbb) sits in this group
O36 wall, M24 south, I9 f
end of column; last group follows the expected text, signs not all identified

units.title: Column 14
units.summary: Second column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (14a 'you alone', 14b Horus / 'my inheritance'); 14c continues the narrative: the two crowns grow on Horus's head and he appears as dual king, uniting the Two Lands in the Wall-nome.

words.note: addressee written against the text direction; D58 (b of Gbb) sits in this group

words.gloss: King of Upper and Lower Egypt

units.title: Column 15
units.summary: Third column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (15a 'to that heir', 15b Horus / 'my inheritance'); 15c narrates that rush and papyrus were set at the double gate of Ptah's house, symbolising Horus and Seth reconciled and united.

words.note: addressee written against the text direction; D58 (b of Gbb) sits in this group

units.title: Column 16
units.summary: Fourth column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (16a 'to the son of my son', 16b Horus / 'the Upper-Egyptian jackal'); 16c continues the narrative: Horus and Seth united in the House of Ptah, the 'Balance of the Two Lands'.

words.note: addressee written against the text direction; D58 (b of Gbb) sits in this group

units.title: Column 17
units.summary: Fifth column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (17a 'one who opened the womb', 17b Horus / 'Opener of the Ways'); 17c, mostly lost, ends with '… of Osiris in the House of Sokar', introducing the story of Osiris's death.

words.note: addressee written against the text direction; D58 (b of Gbb) sits in this group

units.title: Column 18
units.summary: Last column of Geb's speech to the Ennead (18a 'he is a son who was born', 18b Horus / 'on the birthday of Wepwawet'); 18c is almost entirely lost and begins the narrative of Osiris's drowning (Nephthys and Isis 'without delay').

words.note: addressee written against the text direction; D58 (b of Gbb) sits in this group

units.title: Column 19
units.summary: Full-height narrative line continuing 18c: Osiris has drowned in 'his water', Isis (and Nephthys) see it; after the millstone gap the line ends with the order that the goddesses keep him from sinking (ḫw.sn mḥ.f). Paralleled by l. 62.

words.note: lacuna, approx. 1380–2670 (Nephthys; Horus commands them to grasp Osiris)

units.title: Column 20
units.summary: 20a (upper half-line): Horus speaks to Isis and Nephthys, ordering them to grasp Osiris (names written before ḏd-mdw, read after). 20b (lower half): narrative, the goddesses bring Osiris to land (cf. l. 63).

words.note: written after the addressee names (graphic transposition)
reading after Sethe; individual signs uncertain
20b: reading from parallel l. 63; signs mostly traces

units.title: Column 21
units.summary: 21a: Isis and Nephthys speak to Osiris: 'we come, we take you' (layout parallel to 20a). 21b: narrative; Osiris comes into the earth in the Royal Fortress — the last surviving sign (m, 'in') leads into col. 22.

units.title: Column 22
units.summary: Full line, continuing 21b: '… in the Royal Fortress, on the north side [of this land …]'. Most of it is lost; the lower end begins the next episode (building of the fortress, ending at the top of 23).

words.note: written with the fortress ideogram only

units.title: Column 23
units.summary: Full line: end of the narrative of Osiris' burial — 'it happened that the Royal Fortress was built' — after which the rest of the line is lost.

units.title: Column 24
units.summary: 24a: start of a speech by Geb to Thoth (24a–35a), apparently about the Wall/Memphis; 24b (lost) held a short narrative. Breasted did not mark the register division here (Sethe: an oversight).

units.title: Column 25
units.summary: 25a belongs to Geb's speech to Thoth (24a–35a; lost here). 25b–26b: a speech addressed to Isis, of which only scraps survive.

units.title: Column 26
units.summary: 26a: Geb's speech to Thoth (lost). 26b: end of the short speech to Isis (25b–26b); scraps only.

units.title: Column 27
units.summary: 27a: Geb's speech (lost). 27b: short narrative — '[it happened that] Isis caused [someone] to be brought' (Sethe), introducing her address to Horus and Seth in 28b–35b.

words.note: reading from Sethe; the signs on the stone are traces only

units.title: Column 28
units.summary: 28a: Geb's speech (lost). 28b: start of Isis' admonition to Horus and Seth (28b–35b), urging them to make peace (Sethe).

units.title: Column 29
units.summary: 29a: Geb's speech (lost). 29b: Isis' admonition to Horus and Seth continues; several short horizontal signs survive in the upper part of 29b.

words.note: Isis to Horus and Seth; not legible

units.title: Column 30
units.summary: Column 30b: one of the short speech columns (28b-35b) under the a/b divider in which Isis exhorts Horus and Seth to make peace; 30a above the divider is entirely lost.

words.note: Sethe restores a negation 'not will be pleasant'
flat sign over N35 = tn per Sethe

units.title: Column 31
units.summary: Column 31: end of 31a carries the 'wall' sign (inb, 'the Wall', i.e. Memphis) of the Geb–Thoth dialogue; 31b continues Isis's exhortation ('… him, that he may dry your tears', Sethe).

words.note: end of the 31a scenic note, after Sethe

units.title: Column 32
units.summary: Column 32: 32a ends with the 'wall' sign (Sethe), part of a sentence that runs on in the Geb–Thoth dialogue; 32b is the heading plus initial ḏ(d) of another line of Isis's speech, whose rest is destroyed by the millstone socket.

units.title: Column 33
units.summary: Column 33b: one of the short speech columns of Isis's exhortation to Horus and Seth (28b-35b); only the heading and the first sign (ḏ of ḏd 'says') survive above the millstone socket. 33a is lost.

words.note: start of an Isis speech line

units.title: Column 34
units.summary: Column 34b: one of the short speech columns of Isis's exhortation to Horus and Seth (28b-35b); only the heading and the first sign (ḏ of ḏd 'says') survive above the millstone socket. 34a is lost.

words.note: start of an Isis speech line

units.title: Column 35
units.summary: Column 35b: one of the short speech columns of Isis's exhortation to Horus and Seth (28b-35b); only the heading and the first sign (ḏ of ḏd 'says') survive above the millstone socket. 35a is lost.

words.note: start of an Isis speech line

units.title: Column 36
units.summary: Column 36: start of the narrative that follows the dialogues (Erman's Ch); the only surviving words are 'the royal fortress' (a framed figure) and b(w) pn 'this place' (Sethe).

units.title: Column 37
units.summary: Column 37: continuation of the narrative (Erman's Ch); Sethe reads only a bird, n and a stroke near the middle. The column is otherwise destroyed by the socket.

units.title: Column 38
units.summary: Column 38: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 39
units.summary: Column 39: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 40
units.summary: Column 40: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 41
units.summary: Column 41: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 42
units.summary: Column 42: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 43
units.summary: Column 43: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 44
units.summary: Column 44: part of the narrative between the dialogues and the theological section (Erman's Ch / C i); nothing legible survives.

units.title: Column 45
units.summary: Column 45: beginning of the closing passage of the narrative that leads into the theology: 'Great and mighty is the lord who is in …' (compare col. 53 'great and mighty is Ptah').

words.note: reading after Sethe; only the horizontal bar is visible

units.title: Column 46
units.summary: Column 46: continuation of the closing narrative; Sethe reads a single sign sm3 'united (?)' at the head of the column, which Breasted omits.

words.note: after Sethe; the identification is not secured by the photo

units.title: Column 47
units.summary: Column 47: last column of the narrative before the Ptah list (48-52); only the opening survives, read by Sethe as 'entirely' (r-ḏr.f).

words.note: after Sethe ('ganz'); the order and role of 47.2 and 47.4 are unclear

units.title: Columns 48–52
units.summary: Tabular section. A horizontal heading (l.48) 'the gods who took form in Ptah' sits over four sub-columns (49-52), each with an upper entry (a: name, then a shrine with a standing Ptah figure as determinative, then an epithet below the shrine) and a lower entry (b) of which only the ends survive near the bottom of the stone.

words.gloss: who came into being / took form

words.note: only one clear oval; rest restored from Breasted/Sethe
V30 clear; sun-disc for rꜥ may be 48-52.76 shared/second disc not seen

units.title: Column 53
units.summary: Opening of the theology proper: a twin (split) column 'there came into being in the heart / there came into being on the tongue' something in the form of Atum; then 'great and mighty is Ptah', who gave [life/power to all the gods] and their kas through this heart and this tongue.

words.note: three signs before m tjt; unread

units.title: Column 54
units.summary: Twin top 'Horus took form in it / Thoth took form in it, as Ptah'; then the control of heart and tongue over every limb, because the heart is in every body and the tongue in every mouth of all gods, people, cattle and creeping things that live, thinking and commanding whatever it wishes.

words.translit: [m ꜥwt nbt ḥr sbꜣ ntt sw] …
words.gloss: [over every limb, according to the teaching that it is] …
words.note: traces; restored from the expected text

units.title: Column 55
units.summary: His Ennead before him is teeth and lips, i.e. the semen and hands of Atum: the Ennead of Atum came into being through his semen and fingers, but the Ennead is (really) the teeth and lips in this mouth that pronounced the name of everything, from which Shu and Tefnut came forth.

words.gloss: came into being from his semen
(is) the teeth and lips in this mouth
from which Shu and Tefnut came forth

units.title: Column 56
units.summary: End of 'which bore the Ennead'; then the senses: the sight of the eyes, hearing of the ears, breathing of the nose report to the heart, which brings forth every understanding, and the tongue repeats what the heart has devised; so all the gods were born, Atum and his Ennead.

words.gloss: they send up to the heart
words.note: tentative, X8 may belong to the next clause

words.gloss: it is it (the heart) that makes every understanding come forth
it is the tongue that repeats what the heart devises

words.translit: ḫpr ms nṯrw nbw Tm ḥnꜥ psḏt.f
words.gloss: thus were born all the gods, Atum and his Ennead
words.note: scarab, flags and nb clear; detailed alignment tentative

units.title: Column 57
units.summary: Creation by the word: every divine word came about through what the heart devised and the tongue commanded; so the kas and the hemsut were made, which provide all food and offerings, by this word; justice/injustice, life to the peaceful and death to the wrongdoer; then (end of column) all work and crafts, the doing of the arms and the going of the feet.

units.title: Column 58
units.summary: Continues the 'heart and tongue' theology: the movement of every limb follows the command devised by the heart and uttered by the tongue; then Ptah is proclaimed maker of Atum and creator of the gods, Tatenen from whom all food and offerings came.

words.note: Sethe treats wḏ ꜥ md.t as corrupt for wḏ-mdw

words.gloss: who brought the gods into being

words.note: left-hand member of the paired words; spelling partly lost
right-hand member (loaf / p traces); paired side by side with ḏfꜣ.w

units.title: Column 59
units.summary: Ptah's supremacy is recognised and he 'rests' (ḥtp) content after making everything and every divine word; then the founding acts begin: he bore the gods, made the towns, founded the nomes and installed the gods.

words.note: Breasted read this ibis as Thoth

units.title: Column 60
units.summary: Ptah organises the cult: he establishes the gods' offerings, founds their shrines and makes their bodies to their liking; the gods then enter their bodies of every wood, stone and clay and of everything that grows upon him.

words.note: ends the word 'cult-places' begun in col. 59
Breasted's three shrine signs not verifiable
D21 (33) and F34 (36) secure; others tentative

units.title: Column 61
units.summary: The gods and their kas gather to Ptah, who is lord of the Two Lands; Memphis, the 'Great Seat' and granary of the god in the House of Ptah, is described as the source of the Two Lands' sustenance.

words.note: worn; reading after Sethe, not verifiable on the stone

words.gloss: united … lord of the Two Lands
the granary of the god is the Great Seat

units.title: Column 62
units.summary: Explains Memphis' role: Osiris drowned in its water while Isis and Nephthys watched; they saw him and were dismayed, and Horus ordered Isis and Nephthys to take hold of Osiris quickly and stop him from drowning.

words.note: tentative alignment; water/pool sign at end

units.title: Column 63
units.summary: Isis and Nephthys bring Osiris to land; he enters the secret gates in the glory of the lords of eternity, following the one who shines in the horizon, on the ways of Re in the Great Seat.

words.note: the register-like sign (31) may be the gate/door group

words.gloss: (in the dignity of) the lords of eternity
words.note: nḥḥ group at y≈2017–2062 is clear

words.gloss: on the ways of Re in the Great Seat

units.title: Column 64
units.summary: Final column: Osiris enters the earth in the royal fortress on the north side of the land; his son Horus appears as king of Upper and Lower Egypt in the embrace of his father Osiris, among the gods before and behind him.

words.gloss: so Osiris came into the earth

words.translit: ḥr gs mḥtj n tꜣ pn spr.n.f r.f (?)
words.gloss: on the north side of this land, to which he had come
his son Horus appeared as king of Upper Egypt

words.translit: ḫꜥ m bꞽty m ḥnw ꜥwy ꞽt.f Wsꞽr (?)
words.gloss: appeared as king of Lower Egypt in the arms of his father Osiris
among the gods who are before him and behind him
